newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Independent offer may meet resistance - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: Independent offer may meet resistance - NZ Herald.

text.p: The sweetened offer by the Dublin-based Independent Newspapers for Wilson and Horton Ltd may have softened opposition to the takeover bid but it still could find it hard to get to 100 percent, W&H's New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.
It is estimated that as much as 10 percent of the W&H share register is held by investors unwilling to sell at virtually any price.
John Rowley, of broker SBC Warburg, said history had shown that Wilson and Horton shareholders were extremely long-term investors.
"You might have to actually prise the shares out of some people to get them to sell," he said.
This indicated that Independent would have to get to 90 percent and impose compulsory acquisition.
Sun Alliance, a typical long-term shareholder, said that its desired outcome was for W&H to remain listed.
"I think NZ$11.00 a share is a fair price but at a fair price we are still wanting to be shareholders," said Sun's share manager, Darryl Rowell.
Several institutions said the expertise within the Irish company made Wilson and Horton appear an attractive asset. It would also be a hard asset to replace in a portfolio.
The bid, which was raised from NZ$10.50 to $11.00 a share on Monday, is set to begin on Thursday and will remain open for at least a month.

A possible lure for early acceptance is the limited number of exchangeable convertible shares, which are being offered on a first-come, first-served basis and convert into cash or Independent Newspapers shares in seven years.
Some analysts place a value of well over NZ$12.00 on the shares, following the adjustment of the conversion ratio from 1.3125 to 1.375 to reflect the increased cash offer.
A number of institutions have indicated an interest in accepting the exchangeable share offer.
A tax ruling on the treatment of dividends on the shares will see them carry full imputation tax credits.
